slices.focus: Hired outside help finishes first-floor renovation, making the house livable and reducing mental noise
slices.summary: After two years of eating around drop cloths, Derek finally hires outside help to finish the first-floor drywall and clear an electrical punch-list. The expense tightens cash flow again, but the immediate result — a usable, calm first floor — reduces mental noise for the whole family. He realizes that he had been normalizing inconvenience and that the lingering closeout tasks were the real bottleneck. He decides to pause major work on the second floor for a while, framing future spending around three criteria: usable space, time back, or less physical strain.
open_loops: Absorbing the budget hit from paying outside help without overcorrecting
Pausing second-floor work to enjoy the first-floor completion
Sorting future house tasks into: only-him, energy-allows, hire-out
Resisting the temptation to immediately start the next renovation project
decisions: The Brookline row house first floor is now substantially finished and much less chaotic, making the home feel usable ins
The household cash flow tightened again because they paid outside help to push the first-floor renovation through.
